summary: M4-S03 compile run (build-doc-keeper, compile mode) for build northwind-sales: wrote the four declared outputs under artefacts/M4-S03/ from the per-step workbook slices, traceability.md, decisions.md and plan.json, and opened no metadata artefact. The ten-section workbook (67 rows, plus a descope ledger and a 43-row Assumptions Register) passes check_workbook.py at exit 0. The 26-row matrix fails check_rtm.py at exit 1 on the one pre-existing REQ-010 gap, with orphans cut from 19 to 0. The acceptance criteria (77; 76 in the lintable record) pass check_ac_format.py at exit 0. The 63-case UAT pack fails check_uat_case.py at exit 1, because no source gives REQ-004, REQ-016, REQ-017 or REQ-018 a negative case. check-outputs is ok.
confidence_rationale: Step 11 compile rubric: every depends_on step was documented, every declared output was written, and no requirement lacks a step (the HIGH conditions), but four sections compiled with no slice rows (Sections 4, 7, 9 and 10, MEDIUM), six declared outputs have no row in any source, and two of the four declared checkers exit 1 on gaps in the sources.

process_observations.observation: Every depends_on step was documented and gates G3, G4 and G5 recorded a written disposition for the open items they carried, which made each of the 73 decisions.md O- entries classifiable as a case, closed, decided, process or library item without guessing.

Normalizing the renderer rows from plan.json outputs[] and acceptance_tests[] and from results.json took check_rtm.py from 6 errors and 19 orphans on the per-step matrix to 1 error (REQ-010) and 0 orphans on the compiled one.
plan.json scale 'project' matches the clarifier's printed sizing line (D=8, S=9, O=3, integration=no; no override).

No manual test and no open item anywhere in the build states a check that proves REQ-004 (Enterprise record type), REQ-016 (Enterprise Path), REQ-017 (Renewal Path) or REQ-018 (Path preference) blocks a wrong action, so the UAT pack fails negative-path coverage for all four. The negatives the pack does carry are mostly document-level exclusions; the functional denials (rule blocks a rep, second submit refused) come only from open items and M3 test reviews.

Three manual tests still rest on 'M2-S04 ships nothing' or 'M2-S04 is blocked' (M4-S03 T6, M4-S04 T5, M4-S02 T6), and M4-S04 T5, executed as written, would require dropping a shipped, org-validated rule from the build manifest; stale clauses also remain in M2-S05 T5, M1-S02 T5 and plan.json scope.in item 7.

Six declared step outputs have no workbook row in any slice: M2-S01's package.xml and deploy-order.md, and M4-S02's Enterprise_Managers group, two folders and package.xml (render_step_docs.py wrote 4 rows for M4-S02's 8 outputs).

process_observations.observation: render_step_docs.py rows reached the compile with empty artefact cells, test_id 'None', a manual test filed as test_type checker (REQ-025), test_result text narrating 'exit 1' and '? exit ?' that results.json contradicts (REQ-021, CWB-AUTO-001/002), 'O-M3S02-01..00' numbering, a '.sfskills/builds/...' path prefix, no section heading in workbook/06-automation.md, and file paths as target_value that silently exempt Section 6 rows from the automation-selection citation rule.

check_workbook.py files every table after the Section 10 heading under 'Data + Migration', because a non-section heading does not end a section; workbook/99-other-configuration.md's preamble and the committed case-onboarding compile both state that rows there are invisible to the linter, which is wrong.

evidence.query: parse_workbook(); fixture with an unresolvable agent under '## Other configuration' reported '[Data + Migration] row OTH-1'

process_observations.observation: No workbook row and no assumption names an individual owner; the only role that resolves to a person anywhere in the build is VP Sales Operations (Pranav), so M4-S03 T5's 'named owner who can close each one' is met with roles unless the gate supplies names.

No criterion in any source is a bulk (200-record) scenario, although both validation rules and the Apex batch submit are volume-sensitive; check_ac_format.py's Gherkin bulk heuristic would be satisfied by any four-digit year in the file rather than by a bulk scenario.

negative_path was judged strictly (true only when the delivered configuration must block, omit or exclude a wrong state); read as exclusions, M4-T5 ('rather than as a migration') and M2-S05-T6 ('proves neither ... nor') would clear the REQ-004 and REQ-018 failures, and the human should decide which reading the gate accepts.

Three M4-S02 rows were re-homed from Other configuration to Section 8 (the canonical section for reports), while agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 4 maps a ui step to Section 2; M3-S01's email templates were left in Other configuration because no canonical section names them.

Five manual tests and one milestone-goal clause name no single requirement (documents, deploy deny-list, nine prerequisites, mock-deploy evidence) and were keyed by a printed rule, four of them to REQ-001; a human may prefer different keys.

agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 10 says the compile run does not set the step's status (the runner does), while the caller's brief assigned this run both the running and the built transitions; the brief was followed and the conflict is recorded here.
